issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'full sensory reliving' suggests highly vivid, poorly contextualized trauma memory, which sits in marked tension with 'I can talk about what happened very easily.' Those two can sometimes coexist, but as a three-item profile with shame on recall they pull in opposing directions and are clinically questionable together.

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: 'Avoid enclosed spaces' is not clearly coherent with the rest of the profile for sexual assault as described here. The threat and memory items center on being followed, danger in unfamiliar places, delays, shame, and vivid reliving; enclosed spaces introduces a more specific situational avoidance that is not supported by the memory/threat content and looks disconnected from the formulation, especially since Triggers is not active in this case.

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'I can talk about what happened very easily' sits in tension with 'When I remember the event I feel intense shame' and 'Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time.' Severe shame and terror on recall usually make disclosure difficult rather than easy, so this combination is clinically questionable within the same node.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Rumination: Revenge: ruminate about how to get even with assailant
issues.explanation: 'Ruminate about how to get even with assailant' is a poor fit with the rest of the profile for this trauma type and patient presentation. The Memory and Threat items emphasize shame, terror, hypervigilance, and avoidance, which is more consistent with fear-based post-assault PTSD; revenge-focused rumination pulls toward a different emotional/cognitive stance and lacks support elsewhere in the profile.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Gambling: I gamble to distract myself or feel excitement
issues.explanation: 'Gambling' is not impossible, but in this profile it is weakly anchored to the rest of the presentation. The dominant active formulation is Memory↔Threat↔Maladaptive Strategies around trauma recollection and danger monitoring after sexual assault; gambling for excitement/distracting oneself is too nonspecific and does not connect clearly to the patient's other selected threat and memory items.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Enclosed Spaces: Enclosed or confined spaces
issues.explanation: 'Avoid Enclosed Spaces' appears to be a trigger/avoidance cue rather than a maladaptive strategy, and it is poorly matched to the rest of the profile. The threat and memory items center on being followed, danger in unfamiliar places, shame, terror, and speechless recall; avoidance of enclosed spaces is a different contextual pattern that is not otherwise supported here.

vignette: Kofi had been a social worker for over two decades, dedicating his life to helping others. But it was a traumatic event from his past that now threatened to unravel everything he had worked for. Five years ago, while attending a conference in another city, Kofi was sexually assaulted by an acquaintance. The details of the attack were forever seared into his mind: the feeling of being trapped, the helplessness, and the shame. As memories of that night resurfaced, Kofi would often become overwhelmed with terror, reliving the same fear he felt during the assault. When this happened, he found himself ruminating about how to get even with his assailant, fantasizing about revenge as a way to regain control. He also tried to push these thoughts out of his mind, attempting to suppress them with varying degrees of success. But the more he pushed, the more they seemed to linger. The shame associated with the memory was another constant companion for Kofi. When recalling the event, he couldn't shake off the feeling that it was somehow his fault, that he should have been able to prevent it. This self-blame made it even harder for him to open up about what happened, and as a result, he struggled to find words to describe the experience. As Kofi navigated his daily life, these memories continued to shape his perceptions of the world around him. He started to notice potential threats everywhere - every stranger on the street became a possible assailant, every unfamiliar place a potential trap. When walking home from work, he frequently looked over his shoulder, checking if someone was following him. His avoidance of enclosed or confined spaces grew more pronounced, and even simple tasks like grocery shopping became daunting ordeals. When delays occurred in his daily routine - whether it was a traffic jam or a delayed appointment - Kofi's mind would immediately jump to the worst-case scenario: something bad is happening, he thought, my assailant has found me. This hypervigilance had become so ingrained that even small setbacks triggered a cascade of catastrophic thinking. Kofi's avoidance behaviors had also started to affect his work as a social worker. He began turning down cases involving victims of assault or abuse, unable to confront the memories and emotions these situations stirred up in him. His colleagues noticed a change in him - he was more withdrawn, less confident in his abilities - but Kofi couldn't explain what was happening. As the months went by, Kofi's relationships suffered too. His wife grew increasingly frustrated with his moodiness, his inability to connect on an intimate level. She sensed that something was wrong, but Kofi pushed her away, ashamed of his weakness. He knew he needed help but felt trapped in a cycle of fear and avoidance. One evening, as he was walking home from work, Kofi caught himself checking behind him for the umpteenth time. In that moment, he realized how exhausting this constant hypervigilance had become. The memories still lingered, the shame still burned, but something inside him shifted - a spark of recognition that it was time to confront these demons head-on, rather than trying to outrun them forever. It was this glimmer of awareness that finally led Kofi to seek help, driven by a desire to break free from the suffocating grip of his memories and reclaim control over his life. As he sat in the therapist's office, ready to confront the darkness within him, Kofi felt a flicker of hope - maybe, just maybe, he could learn to live with these memories without being consumed by them.
